## TL;DR

A task branch's diff must contain only that task's own files, but several
handoff paths made commits in a task worktree with a bare `git commit` (no
pathspec) or an over-broad `git add -A`. Whatever a concurrent board write had
left staged — another task's `work/<id>-*.md` or `work/reports/<id>/**` — got
folded into the branch, and landing then failed with "the diff changes another
task's bookkeeping". The worst case was the self-check WIP checkpoint, which
re-committed the sibling on every check, so the engineer restored it by hand
round after round.

This change makes every commit boundary in a task worktree pathspec-scoped (or
unstages foreign paths before a bare commit where git forbids a pathspec), reads
the foreign set from the git index rather than the dirty list, and adds a
handoff-time restore that puts main's copy of any foreign bookkeeping back as a
single bookkeeping commit before the review lock.

Review pass 2 left five items open: the committed `done.ts` dist drop that was a
silent pathspec no-op, the lockfile merge that still swept siblings, criterion 1's
documentation-only status (answered by the task's "Accepted scope"), the
`check-remote-wip.test.ts` conflict with main, and a handoff test that exercised
the restore helper rather than handoff. All five are now resolved and committed
at HEAD, and `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD main` is clean.

## Work and rationale

The root defect was a class, not one bad line: any `git commit` in a task
worktree without `-- <paths>` commits the whole index, and every unscoped
`git add -A` stages everything. Since the server writes board bookkeeping
continuously and a worktree is a normal checkout, the index could hold a
sibling's file at any commit. We fixed the class, not one instance.

- **`commitWipCheckpointForRemoteGate`** (`engineer-remote-self-check.ts`) now
  reads foreign paths from the index via `stagedForeignBookkeepingPaths` in
  addition to the dirty list, `git reset HEAD -- <foreign>` to unstage them, and
  commits with `git commit -m <msg> -- <toCommit>`. The earlier version built the
  foreign list only from `uncommittedWorkFiles`, whose filter treats every
  `work/` path as generated — so the set was always empty and the reset never
  ran. Reading the index directly fixes that.
- **`restoreForeignTaskBookkeepingFromMain`** (`core/git.ts`) makes main's copy
  authoritative for foreign `work/` files the branch touched: modified/deleted
  get main's version back, branch-added are removed (`git rm -f`, since a dirty
  copy makes plain `git rm` refuse and abort handoff). Its own commit is
  pathspec-scoped so it never sweeps the task's own staged work, and it prefers
  the recorded `branch.<name>.merge-base` over `merge-base <base> HEAD`.
- **`handoff.ts`** calls the restore after the commit gate and before the review
  lock, and reports what it restored via `onTaskLog` instead of failing.
- **`review-guard.ts`** uses the shared `foreignTaskBookkeepingPaths`, so foreign
  `work/reports/<id>/*.json` (not just `.md`) is dropped, and its implement
  commit is pathspec-scoped.
- **`dropDistBeforeMerge`** (`core/git.ts`, extracted from `done.ts`): the dist
  drop keeps a bare commit (a pathspec commit cannot carry `git rm --cached`,
  which leaves the files untracked — `commit -- dist/` is a silent no-op) after
  unstaging any foreign bookkeeping.
- **`lockfile-conflict.ts`**: `tryCompleteMergeByRegeneratingLockfile` takes an
  optional `{ taskId, filter }`, unstages foreign `work/` paths, then keeps the
  bare `--no-edit` (git rejects a pathspec commit mid-merge). `mergeBranch`
  threads the task id and filter through from `integration-orchestrator.ts`.
- **Criterion 1** is documentation: the server does not deliberately write a
  sibling's file into a worktree (activity/CTO/watchdog and the `syncTaskBranch`
  copy all target `config.root`/main); siblings arrive via merges and the
  unscoped commit boundaries above. `docs/agent-workflow-rules.md` spells this
  out and `AGENTS.md` carries the one-line rule.

## Approaches tried

First I considered filtering only in the checkpoint, since that was the reported
trigger. That would have left `review-guard.ts`'s implement commit and the
merge-of-main lockfile commit able to fold a sibling in — the same loop one path
over. The review's own bug list named those siblings, confirming the class fix.

For the restore I first planned to leave a dirty branch-added sibling "for the
commit gate", but the gate unstages `.md` siblings rather than committing them,
so the copy stayed dirty and handoff failed on exactly the drift the task
targets. Forcing the removal (`git rm -f`) is correct: a task never keeps another
task's bookkeeping.

For the checkpoint's foreign set I tried extending the dirty filter, then
realised the filter is intentionally broad (all `work/` is generated/runtime),
so the only reliable source is `git diff --cached --name-only`.

For the lockfile merge I verified the review's premise in a scratch repo: a
sibling staged *before* the merge cannot reach the commit, because git refuses to
start a merge over a dirty index ("Your local changes would be overwritten by
merge"). The reachable window is *during* the multi-minute `bun install` between
conflict detection and the commit, so I added the unstage there and a test whose
fake `bun` stages a sibling during `install`.

## Challenges and blockers

The trickiest part was proving the restore is wired into handoff, not just a
callable helper. The earlier test called `restoreForeignTaskBookkeepingFromMain`
directly; the reviewer flagged that gap. A full server test is heavy, so I drove
the exported `finalizeReviewHandoff` (the route every non-agent review transition
uses) with `skipChecks: true` and a seeded engineering report — the shape the
existing handoff-unification tests use. It asserts the sibling is gone from
`main...HEAD`, the task-scope preflight passes afterwards, and the task reaches
`review`.

Criterion 1 could have meant a write-site change, but no write site is
deliberately guilty; the honest fix documents the indirect mechanisms and closes
every commit boundary, recorded in the task's "Accepted scope (criterion 1)".

Two environment snags, both non-code: the shell exported `REPOOS_TASK_ID=1073`
from a sibling runner, so `repoos check` acquired the wrong task's gate lock; I
re-ran with `REPOOS_TASK_ID=1076`. Tracked files go read-only under the check
gate, so the formatter needed a `chmod u+w` before it could rewrite the test.

## Key learnings

- A bare `git commit` in a worktree is a category of bug: treat every commit in a
  task worktree as needing a pathspec, and every `add -A` the same.
- A pathspec commit is NOT a drop-in for a bare one: after `git rm --cached` the
  files remain on disk untracked, so `commit -- <deleted paths>` sees nothing.
  There, keep the commit bare and scope the *unstage* instead.
- Git will not start a merge over a dirty index, which bounds where a "sweep at
  merge commit" bug can occur — verify reachability in a scratch repo before
  writing a fix. The real window is a long-running step inside the merge
  (`bun install`), not the merge start.
- The dirty-file filter and the index are different views. Code that must act on
  "what a commit would carry" has to read `git diff --cached`, because the
  filtering helpers deliberately hide `work/`.
- A heal path must not itself use the unsafe pattern it exists to fix.
- Test the wiring, not just the unit: the value of the restore is that handoff
  runs it before the review lock.
